question: Who discovered the sea route to India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vasco da Gama.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vasco-da-Gama**

 
 
• Vasco-da-Gama a Portuguese explorer** discovered the sea route to India** in** 1498. **
 
• His initial voyage to India by way of the **Cape of Good Hope.**
 
• He was the first to link Europe and Asia by an ocean route, connecting the Atlantic and the Indian oceans.
 
• Da Gama's discovery of the sea route to India opened the way for an age of global imperialism.
 
• It enabled the Portuguese to establish a long-lasting colonial empire along the way from Africa to Asia. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Christopher Columbus**

 
 
• **​**Christopher Columbus was an **Italian explorer and navigator.**
 
• He completed four Spanish-based voyages across the Atlantic Ocean sponsored by the Catholic Monarchs of Spain.
 
• He opened the way for the widespread European exploration and colonization of the Americas.
 
• His expeditions were the first known European contact with the Caribbean, Central America, and South America.
 
 
 
• **Ibn Battuta**
 
 
• Ibn Battuta **​**was a **Berber Maghrebi scholar and explorer.**
 
• He traveled extensively in the lands of Afro-Eurasia.
 
• He visited most of southern Eurasia, including Central Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia, China, and the Iberian Peninsula. 
 
 
 
• **Hsuan Tsang**
 
 
• Hsuan Tsang was a 7th-century Chinese **Buddhist monk**, scholar, traveler, and translator.
 
• He is known for the epoch-making contributions to **Chinese Buddhism.**
